narrative.title: One Flat Index over a Serialized Grid
narrative.scenario: A telemetry archive serializes its readings into a grid where every row continues the previous one in ascending order - flattening the grid would yield one sorted list. Storage limits forbid materializing that flattened copy, so the lookup must address cells directly through arithmetic on a virtual flat index.
narrative.inputFormat: An m x n matrix where each row is sorted and the first integer of each row is greater than the last integer of the previous row, plus an integer target.
narrative.outputFormat: true when target appears in the matrix, otherwise false.
constraints: An O(log(m * n)) algorithm is required

testCases.explanation: The virtual flat index resolves to the cell in row 0, column 1, which holds 3.
13 falls between serialized blocks and never matches any probed cell, so the search reports false.

hintLevels: Level 1: Imagine the grid unrolled into one sorted line of length rows times columns and search that line.
Level 2: Convert any flat position back into a cell with integer division and modulo by the column count, then run the classic halving loop on those cells.
Level 3: The conversion must use the column count for both operations, and the loop bounds run from 0 to rows times columns minus 1 so the final row is never skipped.
